hook: Denis Yarats pursued a PhD in artificial intelligence at New York University, focusing on reinforcement learning, and collaborated with Facebook AI Research on projects including end-to-end learning for negotiation dialogues. His research produced DrQ and DrQ-v2, data-augmented reinforcement learning algorithms for training vision-based agents efficiently, and Proto-RL, a self-supervised method using prototypical representations. In August 2022 he co-founded Perplexity AI with Aravind Srinivas, Johnny Ho, and Andy Konwinski, taking on the role of Chief Technology Officer. As CTO, he has helped build the technical infrastructure behind Perplexity's search-grounded answer engine, which launched publicly in December 2022.

reading.body:
Denis Yarats moved from reinforcement learning research to building search infrastructure at Perplexity AI, shifting from improving sample efficiency to scaling inference over real-time web data.

His PhD work on DrQ and DrQ-v2 focused on a narrow, acute problem: making vision-based agents learn from fewer training examples. This work was foundational but bounded. As CTO at Perplexity, launched publicly in December 2022, he now builds systems that must handle scale in a different direction: serving many users querying live web content and generating cited answers in real time. Both roles involve reducing waste in machine learning, but one optimizes training and the other optimizes inference and retrieval.

Perplexity's architecture requires integration across compute allocation, model serving, and real-time search indexing. The shift from his earlier research suggests that once core RL techniques mature, the constraint moves upstream: from algorithmic efficiency to infrastructure that can execute those algorithms reliably at user-facing scale. This is less about inventing new methods and more about orchestrating existing ones through fast, power-hungry systems.

The data does not cover the compute resources Perplexity requires, the power consumption of its infrastructure, or how frequently it refreshes indexed web content. It also does not explain why search-grounded answers require different technical decisions than pure language model inference, though the real-time requirement is noted.

standing.watch: What is unresolved is almost entirely the litigation. Eight cases against Perplexity AI, Inc. sit at the filed stage with docket monitoring active and no development recorded, so the next visible step would be any entry this tracker logs for SyteMLLabs, Sues, Gagleard, Noel, Cable News Network, Amazon.com Services, or The New York Times Company. The records carry no hearing dates, rulings, or settlements, and no outcome for any of them. On the company side, the funding and valuation fields for Perplexity are empty, so nothing in the records points to a planned listing, a raise, or a corporate milestone. Nothing in the supplied records describes Yarats's own next move, and the file does not say whether he is named in any of the cases.
standing.record: The records add up to a short arc: academic reinforcement learning research, collaboration with Facebook AI Research on dialogue and negotiation projects, then co-founding and running the technology of Perplexity. The company entries are thin, showing only a founding year and a San Francisco location, with no funding or valuation recorded. The litigation record is the heavier side of the file, listing eight suits naming Perplexity AI, Inc., including actions from Amazon.com Services, Cable News Network, and The New York Times Company, along with SyteMLLabs, Sues, Gagleard, and Noel. Every one of these is marked as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded by this tracker. The pattern is a young company accumulating filed cases across different plaintiffs while none of the dockets show movement yet.
standing.standing: Denis Yarats stands as co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Perplexity AI, a San Francisco startup founded in August 2022 with Aravind Srinivas, Johnny Ho, and Andy Konwinski. The site lists Perplexity twice in his company records, once as founded and once as a company where he is an executive, with funding and valuation fields left empty. His influence rests on the technical infrastructure behind Perplexity's search-grounded answer engine, which launched publicly in December 2022. Before that he was a PhD researcher in reinforcement learning at New York University, and the records credit him with DrQ and DrQ-v2 and with Proto-RL. The records give no ownership figures, board seats, or other roles beyond the CTO title.
